sn.e: It is Monday morning.
Doña Carmen fills the pila.

sn.s: Llena la pila con una manguera.
sn.e: She fills the pila with a hose.
She fills two buckets as well.
She fills everything she can.
"Why are you filling so much?" I ask.
"Because there is water today," she says.
"And tomorrow there is no water?"
"Tomorrow I do not know," doña Carmen says.
Roberto explains it to me afterwards.

sn.s: "El agua no viene todos los días."
sn.e: "The water does not come every day."
"It comes on Monday and Thursday."
"Sometimes it comes on another day."

sn.s: "A veces no viene en toda la semana."
sn.e: "Sometimes it does not come all week."
"That is why you fill the pila."
Now I understand the pila.

sn.s: La pila no es para bañarse.
sn.e: The pila is not for bathing in.

sn.s: La pila es para guardar el agua.
sn.e: The pila is for storing the water.

sn.s: El lunes se llena la pila.
sn.e: On Monday you fill the pila.

sn.s: El jueves se llena la pila otra vez.
sn.e: On Thursday you fill the pila again.

sn.s: Entre lunes y jueves hay que cuidar el agua.
sn.e: Between Monday and Thursday you have to look after the water.

sn.s: Esa semana yo no cuido el agua.
sn.e: That week I do not look after the water.

sn.s: Lavo mi ropa con mucha agua.
sn.e: I wash my clothes with a lot of water.
I use three buckets of water.

sn.s: Después me baño con dos baldes más.
sn.e: Then I bathe with two more buckets.

sn.s: En la tarde la pila está casi vacía.
sn.e: By the afternoon the pila is nearly empty.
Doña Carmen sees the pila.
She says nothing.
But I see her face.
"Did I do something wrong?" I ask.

sn.s: "Es jueves hasta pasado mañana", dice ella.
sn.e: "It is Thursday the day after tomorrow," she says.
Then I understand.
There is water for today.

sn.s: Y no hay agua para mañana.
sn.e: And there is no water for tomorrow.
And there is still a day to go.
"Sorry, doña Carmen," I say.
"Do not worry, mijo."
"You learn," she says.

sn.s: Esa noche me baño con medio balde.
sn.e: That night I bathe with half a bucket.
Half a bucket is enough.
It is not comfortable, but it is enough.

sn.s: El miércoles no hay agua en la pila.
sn.e: On Wednesday there is no water in the pila.

sn.s: Doña Carmen saca agua de un balde guardado.
sn.e: Doña Carmen takes water from a bucket she kept.

sn.s: Ese balde estaba escondido en la cocina.
sn.e: That bucket was hidden in the kitchen.
She always keeps one bucket back.
Always.

sn.s: "¿Y si viene el agua el jueves?", pregunto.
sn.e: "And if the water comes on Thursday?" I ask.
"Then we fill up again," she says.
On Thursday I get up early.
Very early, with doña Carmen.

sn.s: El agua viene a las cinco de la mañana.
sn.e: The water comes at five in the morning.
We fill the pila together.
We fill the buckets.
We even fill a big pot.

sn.s: A las seis el agua se va.
sn.e: At six the water goes.
But the pila is full.

sn.s: Ahora entiendo por qué se levantan temprano.
sn.e: Now I understand why they get up early.

sn.s: En esta calle todos se levantan temprano el jueves.
sn.e: On this street everybody gets up early on Thursday.

sn.s: Toda la semana depende de esa hora.
sn.e: The whole week depends on that hour.

sn.s: Desde ese día cuido el agua.
sn.e: From that day on I look after the water.
Carefully, like them.
